title: C# & .NET
description: Learn C# fundamentals, test reusable logic, and build a small ASP.NET Core task API with safe SQLite persistence.
prerequisites: Comfort using a terminal and editing a text file.
No prior C# experience required; basic HTTP and SQL help with the final lessons.
outcomes: Run and debug C# console projects.
Use types, null checks, collections, methods, objects, LINQ and exceptions.
Await asynchronous operations and write focused unit tests.
Build validated HTTP endpoints with dependency injection and parameterized persistence.
setup: Install the current patched .NET 10 LTS SDK from Microsoft's download page using the installer for your OS; these instructions do not install software automatically.
Use a text editor or IDE with C# support. Verify dotnet --info and dotnet --list-sdks in a new terminal.
Create a separate console project for snippets with dotnet new console -n LearningConsole -f net10.0; replace Program.cs for each console lesson and run dotnet run.
As of September 26, 2026, Microsoft's policy lists .NET 10 LTS through November 14, 2028. Recheck the policy at study time and keep patches current.
Package-based testing and database lessons require restore access. Examples labeled fragments need the enclosing project described in their lesson.
nextSteps: Study ASP.NET Core integration testing with WebApplicationFactory.
Learn EF Core migrations, relational constraints and transactions.
Add authentication, authorization, structured logging and deployment only after the local capstone works.
Study interfaces, generics and concurrency in greater depth.

lessons.title: Run a C# program
lessons.takeaway: C# is the language; the SDK builds and runs .NET projects.

sections.title: The project and runtime
paragraphs: The SDK includes tools for creating projects, compiling C#, restoring packages and running applications. The runtime executes compiled applications. Installing only a runtime is insufficient for these lessons.

Use the current patched .NET 10 LTS SDK for new work. Check the linked support policy before installation; do not choose a preview just because its number is higher. These lessons use features that also work in .NET 8 and 9, but their support windows differ.
sections.example:
dotnet --info
dotnet new console -n LearningConsole -f net10.0
cd LearningConsole
dotnet run
# Expected: Hello, World!

sections.title: Edit and repeat
paragraphs: Replace Program.cs with the example below. Top-level statements provide the entry point without writing a Program class. Console.WriteLine writes text followed by a newline.

Every console example in lessons 1–8 is a separate complete Program.cs unless labeled otherwise. Do not append all examples to one file. A missing semicolon or a quote without its partner is a compiler error; read the first error and its line before changing unrelated code.
sections.example:
Console.WriteLine("Hello, C#!");
// Expected: Hello, C#!

exercise.prompt: Print your name and one learning goal on separate lines.
checks: dotnet run prints exactly two lines.
Change the name without changing the goal.

quiz.question: Which component is required to compile these projects?
quiz.explanation: The SDK contains the compiler and project tools.

lessons.title: Types, values and missing data
lessons.takeaway: Choose types deliberately and handle null before using a value.

sections.title: Numbers and strings
paragraphs: int represents whole numbers; decimal is useful for decimal money arithmetic; bool represents true or false; string holds text. var asks the compiler to infer a type and does not make a variable dynamically typed.
Integer division discards the fractional part. Use a decimal operand when the fraction matters. The m suffix marks a decimal literal.

sections.title: Null and input
paragraphs: A nullable string, written string?, may contain no string. Console.ReadLine can return null when input ends, so validate before using it. The ?? operator supplies a fallback; ?. accesses a member only when the receiver exists.
Nullable annotations guide compiler analysis; they do not validate user input at runtime. Avoid adding ! just to silence a warning. TryParse handles an expected invalid input without an exception.

exercise.prompt: Parse a quantity and reject missing, invalid or negative values.
exercise.starter:
string? input = "-2";
// Validate and print a message.

quiz.question: What does var change?
options: The compiler infers the fixed type
quiz.explanation: var changes how a type is written, not how the type system works.

lessons.title: Control flow and collections
lessons.takeaway: Use branches for decisions and collections for groups of values.

sections.title: Branch and loop
paragraphs: if selects code based on a boolean condition. foreach visits each item in a collection; it is clearer than manually tracking indexes when you only need values.

An array has a fixed length. List<T> can grow. Generic T specifies the element type so an accidental string cannot enter a List<int>. Do not add or remove items from a list while enumerating it with foreach.

sections.title: Lookup by key
paragraphs: Dictionary<TKey,TValue> associates unique keys with values, useful for looking up a task by its ID. TryGetValue handles a missing key; indexing a missing key throws.
Decide whether duplicate keys should be rejected or replace a value. A loop boundary using <= instead of < can access one element beyond an array.

exercise.prompt: Count passing scores without storing a second collection.
exercise.starter:
var scores = new List<int> { 59, 60, 100 };
int passes = 0;

quiz.question: Which collection supports lookup by an ID key?
quiz.explanation: A dictionary maps keys to values.

lessons.title: Methods and contracts
lessons.takeaway: A method names a small operation with explicit inputs and output.

sections.title: Parameters and return values
paragraphs: A method isolates logic so callers do not repeat it. Parameters are local names for supplied values. A return type describes the result; void means no result.
Prefer returning a computed value over printing inside every method. This lets the same logic support a console, a web endpoint and a test. Local functions below work in a top-level Program.cs.

sections.title: Define invalid inputs
paragraphs: State the method's contract: for example quantity and price must be nonnegative. Validate at the boundary rather than silently producing impossible results.

Parameters are passed by value by default. For a reference type the copied value is a reference, so mutating an object's contents can still affect its caller. Avoid hidden mutation when a return value is enough.

exercise.prompt: Write IsPassing so 60 is the minimum passing score.

quiz.question: Why return a value instead of always printing?
options: It lets callers reuse and test the result
quiz.explanation: Computation can be reused independently of its presentation.

lessons.title: Classes, records and state
lessons.takeaway: Model related data and protect the operations that change it.

sections.title: An object with behavior
paragraphs: A class combines state with operations. A constructor creates a valid instance. Properties expose data; a private setter allows only the class to change a property.
Place class declarations after top-level statements. Public fields make it easy for unrelated code to bypass your rules. A method such as Complete makes the allowed change visible.

sections.title: Records and boundaries
paragraphs: A record is convenient for data represented by values, such as a request body. Positional records generate properties and value-based equality. A class remains useful for an entity whose identity and changing state matter.
An interface describes behavior without prescribing storage. Later an API can depend on a service interface and tests can substitute an implementation. Avoid inheritance merely to share a few lines.

exercise.prompt: Make a task reject a blank title and trim valid titles.
checks: An empty or whitespace title throws ArgumentException.
The Title setter is not public.

quiz.question: What does a private setter enforce?
options: Only code inside the class can assign that property
quiz.explanation: Access control constrains how state changes.

lessons.title: Exceptions and resource cleanup
lessons.takeaway: Handle failures at a boundary and release resources reliably.

sections.title: Expected versus exceptional
paragraphs: A failed TryParse is normal invalid input. An inaccessible file is an operation failure that may throw. Catch an exception only where you can recover or present a useful message.
Catch the specific type you understand. An empty catch hides failures. If you must rethrow the same exception, use throw; so its original stack information is retained.

sections.title: Dispose owned resources
paragraphs: Some objects hold operating-system resources. using ensures Dispose runs even if the operation throws. The scope should be short and ownership clear.
Dispose is not a substitute for handling failure. Do not catch all exceptions and report success; the next layer needs to know whether data was actually saved.

exercise.prompt: Read a supplied file and return a friendly message only when it is missing.
checks: A missing file prints the friendly message.
Other failures are not silently converted to success.

quiz.question: What does using primarily guarantee?
options: Dispose runs when the scope exits

lessons.title: Query collections with LINQ
lessons.takeaway: Compose filtering, ordering and projection without hiding when work executes.

sections.title: A query pipeline
paragraphs: LINQ extension methods work on sequences. Where filters, OrderBy sorts, and Select transforms each item. A lambda such as n => n >= 60 defines the operation for an item.
ToList materializes the result into a list. Many sequence operators are deferred: creating a query does not necessarily enumerate its source. This matters if you mutate the source before enumeration.

sections.title: Choose terminal operations
paragraphs: Any answers whether a match exists and Count counts matches. First throws on an empty sequence; FirstOrDefault supplies a default. For a reference type that default may be null.
LINQ over in-memory collections executes C#. LINQ through a database provider is translated and supports a provider-specific subset. Do not assume every helper method can become SQL.

exercise.prompt: Return even numbers in descending order.
checks: An all-odd input produces an empty list.

quiz.question: Which operator changes each item into another shape?
quiz.explanation: Select projects each source item into a result.

lessons.title: Asynchronous operations and cancellation
lessons.takeaway: await represents waiting for an operation without synchronously blocking the caller.

sections.title: Tasks and await
paragraphs: An async method commonly returns Task or Task<T>. await suspends that method until the operation completes and then retrieves its result or propagates its exception.

Async is especially useful for I/O such as files, HTTP and databases. It does not automatically make CPU work faster or place every method on a new thread. Avoid .Result and .Wait in asynchronous paths.

sections.title: Cancellation is cooperative
paragraphs: CancellationToken lets the caller request cancellation. Pass it through to APIs that accept it. A cancelled operation may throw OperationCanceledException, which can be handled at the boundary.

Use async void only for event handlers that require it; callers cannot await its completion. Await started tasks so their failures are observed. Artificial delay here teaches the mechanism, not network performance.

exercise.prompt: Write a cancellable method that returns 42 after a short delay.
exercise.starter: static async Task<int> LoadAsync(CancellationToken token) { return 0; }

quiz.question: Does async automatically make a CPU calculation faster?
quiz.explanation: Async models waiting; CPU parallelism is a separate decision.

lessons.title: Test reusable logic
lessons.takeaway: A test proves a specific behavior using inputs and assertions.

sections.title: Create separate projects
paragraphs: Put reusable logic in a class library and tests in a test project. The reference lets tests call the library. Package restore requires network access; inspect generated files and package versions rather than assuming templates never change.
These commands create projects, not an entire finished application. A test runner reports failure when an assertion does not match; dotnet build only checks compilation.
sections.example:
dotnet new classlib -n TaskLogic -f net10.0
dotnet new xunit -n TaskLogic.Tests -f net10.0
dotnet add TaskLogic.Tests/TaskLogic.Tests.csproj reference TaskLogic/TaskLogic.csproj
dotnet test TaskLogic.Tests/TaskLogic.Tests.csproj
# Expected: generated test project builds and tests run

sections.title: Assert boundaries
paragraphs: Add the first code block to TaskLogic/Rules.cs and the second to a test file. Tests should cover a normal input and the threshold on both sides. Keep file-system and network dependencies out of a unit test when testing arithmetic or validation.
A passing test is evidence for its cases, not proof that all inputs work. Start with a failing assertion to confirm the test is discovered, then restore the correct expectation.

exercise.prompt: Add a 100-point case and demonstrate one failing test before fixing it.
checks: All three cases pass after correction.
The intentional wrong expectation produces a test failure.
Production logic is not changed to satisfy a wrong expectation.

quiz.question: What does a successful build establish?
quiz.explanation: Compilation and behavior verification answer different questions.

lessons.title: Build an ASP.NET Core API with dependency injection
lessons.takeaway: HTTP endpoints translate requests into service calls and explicit responses.

sections.title: A complete small API
paragraphs: Create an empty ASP.NET Core project, then replace Program.cs with the code below. A GET reads data; a POST accepts a JSON request and returns 201 with a resource location. Request binding constructs the record from JSON.

Use the printed listening address or the explicit URL shown here. Local HTTP is sufficient for this exercise; it is not a deployment recipe. A singleton store holds shared memory and must synchronize access. This example does so, but data disappears on restart.
sections.example:
dotnet new web -n TaskApi -f net10.0
cd TaskApi
# Replace Program.cs with the next section's complete file.
dotnet run --urls http://localhost:5080
# In another terminal:
curl.exe http://localhost:5080/tasks
# Expected initially: []

sections.title: Register and inject a service
paragraphs: Dependency injection creates registered services and supplies them to endpoint parameters. Singleton means one instance for the application; scoped usually means one per request; transient means a new instance per resolution.

Do not inject a scoped database context into a singleton store. The following complete file validates titles and protects its list with a lock; it is intentionally small enough to replace with a persistent store later.

exercise.prompt: Send valid and blank POST requests, then retrieve a missing task.
exercise.starter: # Use an HTTP client with Content-Type: application/json.
exercise.solution:
curl.exe -i -X POST http://localhost:5080/tasks -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data-raw "{\"title\":\"Read\"}"
# Shell quoting varies: an HTTP client or JSON file with --data-binary @request.json avoids escaping issues.
# POST {"title":"  "} => 400; GET /tasks/999 => 404.
checks: Valid POST returns 201 and a Location header.

quiz.question: How long does a singleton service live?
quiz.explanation: Singleton services share application-wide state and require safe concurrency.

lessons.title: Persist data and parameterize queries
lessons.takeaway: Database values belong in parameters, with schema and lifetimes managed explicitly.

sections.title: Use a scoped context
paragraphs: EF Core maps entities to tables and LINQ queries to SQL. In the existing TaskApi project, add the SQLite provider from the 10.x release family that matches this path's target framework. Keep runtime, provider and tooling versions compatible.

Replace the in-memory registration and endpoint implementation rather than mixing both stores. A DbContext is normally scoped to a request and is not thread-safe. Await an operation before starting another on the same context.
sections.example:
dotnet add package Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite --version 10.0.0
# Use a current supported 10.x patch for real projects; 10.0.0 is a reproducible lesson baseline.
# Program.cs fragment; add before builder.Build():
# builder.Services.AddDbContext<TaskDb>(o => o.UseSqlite("Data Source=tasks.db"));

sections.title: A database endpoint fragment
paragraphs: This fragment shows the key pieces, not a complete replacement Program.cs. Add the using directive at the file top, the context and entity after top-level statements, and register the context before building the app. Initialize after building and before app.Run.

EnsureCreated is convenient for an isolated learning database. It does not manage an evolving production schema and should not be mixed with a migrations workflow. Use migrations and review generated changes as the model evolves.

sections.title: Keep SQL and data separate
paragraphs: LINQ predicates let the provider bind input as data. EF Core's interpolated FromSql form also parameterizes values when the interpolated expression is passed directly. Building a SQL string with concatenation and sending it through FromSqlRaw allows input to change SQL structure.
Parameters cannot substitute table names or sort keywords. Choose structural options from a fixed allowlist. Do not log secrets or put database credentials in committed code.

exercise.prompt: Add POST /saved-tasks using validation, Add and SaveChangesAsync; verify persistence after restart.
exercise.starter: // Register TaskDb, then map a POST endpoint.
checks: Restarting from the same working directory preserves the row.
A title such as O'Brien is stored literally.

quiz.question: Which query keeps input as data?
options: Trusting input because it came from JSON
quiz.explanation: The provider parameterizes the predicate's value.

lessons.title: Capstone: a tested task service
lessons.takeaway: Combine contracts, persistence, HTTP responses and tests into a small explainable application.

sections.title: Define observable behavior
paragraphs: Build a task service with create, list, fetch and complete operations. Each task has an integer ID, a trimmed nonblank title and a Done flag. An unknown task returns 404; invalid creation returns 400; valid creation returns 201.

Persist tasks in SQLite and use a scoped context. Add a GET endpoint matching the Location returned by POST. The API should await database calls and pass cancellation through. This is a local learning service; authentication and deployment remain next steps.
sections.example:
POST /tasks {"title":"  Read  "} -> 201 with title Read and done false
GET /tasks/{id} -> 200
PATCH /tasks/{id}/complete -> 204
GET /tasks/{id} -> done true
PATCH /tasks/999/complete -> 404

sections.title: Implement and verify deliberately
paragraphs: Start from the preceding database lesson, remove duplicate in-memory routes and add Done to the entity before creating a fresh learning database or using a reviewed migration. Isolate title validation into a pure method and test blank, whitespace and valid input.

Add HTTP-level checks for status codes and persistence so a correct helper cannot mask a broken route. Do not delete an existing database containing valuable data to work around a schema mismatch. Explain each route, service lifetime and input rule in a short README.

exercise.prompt: Finish the service and write a repeatable acceptance sequence covering creation, completion and restart.
exercise.starter: // Extend SavedTask with Done and use one persistent set of /tasks routes.
checks: dotnet build and dotnet test succeed for your projects.
Blank creation returns 400; valid creation returns 201.
The Location resource can be fetched.
Restart preserves title and completion state.

quiz.question: Why also test the HTTP boundary?
options: A unit-tested helper cannot establish route binding and status behavior
HTTP tests replace all database checks
quiz.explanation: The boundary adds behavior that a pure helper test does not exercise.
